review_text: The early access label is an excuse for a janky game that is constantly getting updates no one asked for. They change what little good the game has, but never change any of the bad, like the giant maps that’re empty. Once playable maps, are now a damn lag simulator, and I don’t even play on that low end of a PC. This game has made about $260 million dollars, yet the studio seems to genuinely mainly care about overpriced merch. The updates are so few and far between, and when they do come, they’re lackluster or worse, do more harm than good by adding bad content and bugs. The dev team for some reason seem to have a bad relationship with the community, and I cannot for the life of me think of any reason why. The reason you guys are STANDING as a team and company is because of fans, but you shut us down and dismiss us, and discourage anything that goes outside of the narrative you guys so desperately want. They’re strongly against mods for the weirdest reason, I mean what the hell man, you would get even more plays and diversity in the game if you allowed or encouraged it. This game was fun and interesting at one point. It was janky, but more so in a lovable way, where you could tell it was a little rough, but made with love. But recently, with all the unnecessary changes, the way the dev team acts towards us, and the way the game is handled as a whole, the past 2 or so years leaves such a bad taste in my mouth, and the game feels more like a chore now than anything. 4/10 for me

review_text: Played for years and it was a nice chill horror game to play with friends The latest update rolls around, and with it came animations with every single interaction, all of which slows down the game dramatically. The quick responsiveness of interactions with things like smudge sticks are a thing of the past with this new update. Now you have to wait a few seconds for everything, and in the heat of the moment against a ghost, those few seconds might as well be a few years. They also added character customization, but only in name. The items that the give you in the way of shirts, hairstyles, and so many other options that you would expect in a character creator are surprisingly limited. Think a max of 3 or 4 outfits regardless of how far you've made it into the game. I won't even get into the character models. This game still has a lot of the charm that made me fall in love with it back in 2021, but this update removed a large portion of that charm, and I honestly cannot recommend anyone spend their money on the game in its current state

review_text: 4 years since I was gifted this and somehow I never reviewed it?? well, better late than never I suppose! Phasmophobia is an intriguing multiplayer supernatural-horror/thriller experience, you play as paranormal investigative contractors- in each contract you play, you have one goal, use your various equipment items (more are unlockable as you progress, and different tiers too!) to identify and confirm the type of supernatural entity residing within whatever haunted location, there's maps such as a prison ,a school, and various different houses. You *can* play it singleplayer, but in my humble opinion, it's far better with friends, even just one other person, though it's good fun for a group! hop on a discord call, or use in-game proximity chat to talk & work together- the gameplay is solid, and all around an engaging, and somewhat addictive experience, and this game is genuinely a labor love, all these years gone by and it's still actively being worked on, it's so much more polished than it was in 2022! Highly recommend, even for non-horror fans!~

review_text: Old Phas - 8.5/10 New Phas- 6.5/10 A pioneer in it's genre with many clones released as a result. Was very fun at launch and would easily make you feel uneasy thinking there's ghosts in your house, and is insane in VR, but lost me around 2022. I enjoy watching it on YouTube more than playing it these days. So many different items to learn and way too many ghost types, you have to memorize a textbook and no-life grind it to learn all the traits and you'll likely get your neck snapped 300 times before you get there. 90% of the time you'll get 2 pieces of evidence and just sit there waiting until the 3rd one appears after half the team is already dead. The most recent new animation update isn't too bad and it seems like the economy was improved a bit but I enjoy going back and playing the early versions from SteamDB more. Trolling around in lobbies is more entertaining than the base game, that is, if you can find a lobby that's not a boosting lobby. If you've never played it before you'll probably enjoy it still though.

review_text: Phasmophobia is exactly the kind of ghost-hunting chaos I want. The problem is that I have no friends to play it with. Which is rude, because this game is clearly built for group panic. I want to walk into a haunted house with a flashlight, a dream, and the confidence of someone who has watched way too much Sam and Colby. I want to ask ghosts disrespectful questions, immediately regret it, and then scream because something moved in the kitchen. The whole setup is so good. You gather evidence, use equipment, watch for signs, try to figure out what kind of ghost you are dealing with, and then attempt to leave before it turns your investigation into a funeral announcement. It is creepy, funny, stressful, and so much better when everyone is panicking together. One person is trying to be serious. One person is already hiding in the van. One person is yelling the ghost’s name like they have never heard of consequences. That is the dream. Even without a full group, I still love the idea of it. The atmosphere is tense, the ghost mechanics are fun, and every investigation feels like it could go from “we are professionals” to “absolutely not, goodbye” in half a second. Phasmophobia lets me live my Sam and Colby dreams, or at least it would if my friends would get their lives together and play with me. Until then, I am just standing outside the haunted house with equipment, trust issues, and no backup.

review_text: Phasmophobia: A Masterclass in Shared Terror If you had told me a few years ago that I’d spend my weekends willingly walking into dark, haunted houses just to get mocked by a demon via a Spirit Box, I would have called you crazy. Yet, here I am, utterly hooked on Phasmophobia. While the game is brilliant as a solo horror experience, it truly transcends into something special when played in co-op. I’ve been playing exclusively with my brother, and it has easily become our favorite gaming ritual. The Joy of Custom Terrors What keeps Phasmophobia so incredibly fresh—even after hours of hunting—is how adaptable it is. Once you get a handle on the basic mechanics, the game gives you the freedom to make your own fun. My brother and I have started cooking up our own custom challenges to test our nerves, like: The "No Flashlight" Challenge: Relying strictly on candles and glowsticks to navigate a massive asylum. The Speed-Run: Trying to identify the ghost and escape within five minutes. The sandbox nature of the difficulty settings allows you to tweak the game to perfectly match your skill level, keeping the tension sky-high. The Thrill of the Hunt (and the Loot) Beyond just surviving, there is a genuine addiction to searching the maps for cursed possessions. There is nothing quite like the chaotic adrenaline rush of finding a deck of Tarot Cards. The dynamic changes instantly: do we play it safe, or do we risk pulling a High Priestess (or worse, the Death card) just for the thrill of it? Hunting down these items, filling up the investigation journal, and snapping perfect photos of the paranormal feels less like a repetitive loop and more like a genuine, eerie treasure hunt. The Verdict Phasmophobia balances genuine, heart-pounding dread with incredible cooperative gameplay. The sound design is top-tier (hearing a ghost breathe right in your ear will never not make you jump), and the proximity chat creates unforgettable moments of panic and comedy. If you have a dedicated gaming partner—like a sibling who is willing to use you as ghost bait—this game is an absolute must-play. It’s scary, it’s chaotic, and it’s some of the most fun you can have in the dark.

Recent updates have been... janky to say the least, and there are inconsistencies with the mechanics that do need addressing. However, the team behind it is actively adding new updates/events pretty consistently, so some turbulence is to be expected. The new character model system has been especially devicive, but don’t let that put you off; as long as you’re not expecting in-depth character customization, you should be fine. At the end of the day, for £16, I feel I’ve gotten way more than my money’s worth out of it and will continue to do so. I hope you do too!
